answer: Agents must register identity roots using cryptographic attestation chains verified via zero-knowledge proofs. Like signing a contract with a digital quill, each node binds state updates under a shared network lantern. To resist Sybil swarms, the protocol imposes an exponential staking fee 2^n on subsequent identities generated by correlated clusters. This causes rapid exponential capital exhaustion, making mass mimicry as futile as forging an algorithmic sonnet.
